chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If you remember while you are in your salat (prayer) that you have left out something from your wudu (ablution) that is obligatory upon you, then leave and complete what you forgot from your wudu, and repeat your salat. And for wiping your head, it is sufficient for you to take from your beard its moisture if you forgot to wipe your head, then wipe with it the front of your head.

key_terms.صَلَاتِكَ: your salat (prayer), the act of worship being invalidated by an incomplete obligatory wudu
key_terms.فَٱنْصَرِفْ: then leave, meaning to break off the current salat
key_terms.لِحْيَتِكَ: your beard, from whose moisture one may take for the wiping
key_terms.مَسْحِ رَأْسِكَ: wiping your head, the prescribed act of masḥ in wudu
key_terms.مُقَدَّمَ رَأْسِكَ: the front of your head, the place to be wiped in wudu
key_terms.وَأَعِدْ: and repeat, referring to performing the salat again after completing wudu
key_terms.وُضُوئِكَ: your wudu (ablution), the ritual purification required before salat
key_terms.ٱلْمَفْرُوضِ: that which is obligatory, referring to the required elements of wudu

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they remember during salat that they missed part of their wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who remembers during salat (prayer) that an obligatory part of wudu (ablution) was omitted. It instructs that the person must leave the prayer, complete the omitted part of wudu, and then repeat the salat, while also stating that the remaining moisture from the beard may be used to perform the wiping of the front of the head.
